Set up. Ground link FG = 3 cm (pivots G and F). Link AG = 5 cm turns about G. The T-link CDEF turns about F, with D at 1.5 cm from F and the slot CE perpendicular to FD. The slider B runs along CE, and AB = 3 cm is held perpendicular to CE.

Step 1 — where can A be? Because AB ⟂ CE and B lies on CE, point A always lies on a line parallel to CE at 3 cm from it. CE itself is 1.5 cm from F, on the opposite side from A, so A's line is 3 − 1.5 = 1.5 cm from F on the other side.

So as the T-link turns through any angle θ, A must lie on a line at a fixed distance of 1.5 cm from F, turning with it.

Step 2 — can the T-link turn fully? A is also on the circle of radius 5 cm about G. The line meets that circle as long as its distance from G is at most 5 cm. The largest possible distance of G from the line is GF + 1.5 = 3 + 1.5 = 4.5 cm < 5 cm. So for every θ there is a valid position of A: CDEF can rotate completely.

Step 3 — the other links. As CDEF goes round, the line (and hence A) goes all the way round G, so AG also rotates fully. AB stays perpendicular to CE, so it turns with CDEF and is fully rotatable too.

Answer: a Grashof-type chain in which AG, AB and CDEF all rotate completely about the ground link FG — option (A).
